land.text: all of Anga: 'Anga became part of the Magadhi empire, and Campa became the seat of a Magadhi viceroy'

successors.note: Bimbisara's Magadha. Cliopatria's Haryanka row (magadha-haryanka-dynasty) begins only in -500, so the land goes to the Janapada of Magadha row alive in -530; the Magadha agent (sa-01) should carry the matching gain in -530 and may merge the two Magadha rows.

capitals.name: Champa (Champapuri, Bhagalpur)
capitals.note: 'located at the confluence of the Champa and Ganga rivers', in the 'modern-day area of Champapuri and Champanagar in Bhagalpur'; coordinates are modern Bhagalpur's. The infobox also names Malini (near modern Munger), Malini being Champa's Puranic name.

correction.text: Anga 'between the Champa river to the west and the Rajmahal hills to the east', with Campa 'at the confluence of the Champa and Ganga rivers' near Bhagalpur and Malini near Munger

keyframe_review.note: The 5,578 km2 shape (bbox 86.75-87.77E, 24.20-25.04N) lies south of the Ganges around Dumka and stops 20 km short of Champa at Bhagalpur (25.25N); the 60 km radius adds the capital and Malini (Munger). The infobox gives no area to compare.

correction.text: the same land, but Magadha's: 'Anga became part of the Magadhi empire' when Bimbisara killed Brahmadatta in the middle of the 6th century BCE (infobox 'Disestablished c. 530 BCE'); the years -530..-501 belong to janapada-of-magadha

keyframe_review.note: Right land, wrong owner: Cliopatria keeps Anga to -501, the page ends it c. 530 BCE.

region.text: Anga 'between the Champa river to the west and the Rajmahal hills to the east', with Campa 'at the confluence of the Champa and Ganga rivers' near Bhagalpur and Malini near Munger

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Anga, easternmost of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, is ruled from Champa. The page lists Anga among the 'sixteen great nations' of the Anguttara Nikaya ('Anga is the easternmost, south of Vajji and east of Magadha') and dates Dadhivahana's reign to the 6th century BCE; -600 is the Mahajanapada convention ('from the sixth to fourth centuries BCE', Mahajanapadas page). The infobox's 'Established: Unknown (~1100 BCE)' is not drawn; the Vedic-era Anga is left to batch sa-01-x.

Early 6th century BCE: Anga under Dadhivahana overruns Magadha. 'Under Dadhivahana's rule, Anga had conquered its western neighbour, the state of Magadha' (6th century BCE), and Brahmadatta later defeated Bimbisara's father; the page gives no years, so the struggle is drawn as a contest over Magadha from -600 until Bimbisara's accession.

543 BCE: Bimbisara takes the Magadhan throne and Magadha is Anga's no longer. 'He ascended to throne at the age of 15 in 543 BCE' (reign 'c. 544 - c. 492 BCE or c. 457 - c. 405 BCE'); the Anga page gives no date for Magadha's recovery, so the contest is closed at his accession.

region.text: Anga 'between the Champa river to the west and the Rajmahal hills to the east', with Campa 'at the confluence of the Champa and Ganga rivers' near Bhagalpur and Malini near Munger

ledger.note: c. 530 BCE: Bimbisara of Magadha kills Brahmadatta and annexes Anga; Champa becomes a viceroy's seat. 'Bimbisara Srenika avenged his father's defeat against Anga by defeating and killing the Angeya king Brahmadatta' in the middle of the 6th century BCE, 'after which Anga became part of the Magadhi empire, and Campa became the seat of a Magadhi viceroy'; infobox 'Disestablished c. 530 BCE'. Bimbisara page: 'Anga was annexed, and prince Kunika (Ajatashatru) was appointed governor at Champa'; Mahajanapadas page: 'Anga was annexed by Magadha in the time of Bimbisara'. Cliopatria keeps Anga to -501.

wars.name: Anga-Magadha wars
wars.outcome: Anga under Dadhivahana conquered Magadha and Brahmadatta defeated Bimbisara's father; Bimbisara then defeated and killed Brahmadatta and annexed Anga (c. 530 BCE).
wars.note: Undated beyond '6th century BCE' and 'the middle of the 6th century BCE'; the Bimbisara page dates his accession to 543 BCE and his reign c. 544-492 (or c. 457-405) BCE.

wars.name: Kalinga's attack on Anga
wars.outcome: 'the state of Kalinga attacked Anga and took Dadhivahana captive'; Udayana 'was able to defeat Kalinga and restore Dadhivahana on the Angeya throne'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Undated; placed in Dadhivahana's 6th-century reign. Kalinga of this period has no Cliopatria row (the Kalinga row is -318..-171).

certainty.note: No frontier is recorded; the shape is the Champa country between the Champa river and the Rajmahal hills.

sources.title: Anga
sources.note: Identity, infobox (~1100 BCE to c. 530 BCE), Champa and Malini, Dadhivahana's conquest of Magadha, Kalinga's attack, Bimbisara's killing of Brahmadatta and the annexation.

sources.title: Bimbisara
sources.note: Reign c. 544-492 or c. 457-405 BCE, accession 543 BCE, the Anga campaign and Kunika as governor at Champa.

sources.title: Mahajanapadas
sources.note: Overview of the sixteen states ('from the sixth to fourth centuries BCE'), the Mahajanapada convention behind every -600 start, and the per-state location notes; shared by the five janapada dossiers of batch sa-01-a.

notes: Cliopatria's two identical shapes (-600..-531, -530..-501) hold the right land about 20 km too far south and keep Anga thirty years after the page ends it (c. 530 BCE); the second shape is marked wrong and its land goes to janapada-of-magadha from -530. The Anga-Magadha struggle before Bimbisara is undated on the page and is drawn as a contest over Magadha at confidence 1 (-600..-543). Unsettled: the infobox's '~1100 BCE' start (the Vedic Anga, for sa-01-x); which Magadha dossier should carry the -530 gain (janapada-of-magadha is the row alive then; the Haryanka row starts -500); Kalinga of the 6th century BCE has no row. Gazetteer: Bhagalpur is present; no new names.
